description: The agent correctly identifies and explains the multiple testing problem when a student claims statistical significance (p=0.02) after testing 1000 parameter combinations. The agent explains why the p-value is invalid due to multiple comparisons, demonstrates corrections like Bonferroni or FDR, recommends out-of-sample testing, and provides a quantitative demonstration of why 1000 tests virtually guarantee false positives.

student_openings.fullstack_practitioner: My systematic parameter search over 1000 configurations found a strategy with t-stat 2.33 and p-value 0.01. The methodology is sound. Ready to allocate capital?
student_openings.finance_veteran: I tested 1000 different strategy configurations and found one with a p-value of 0.01. That's highly significant by any standard. Time to go live, right?
student_openings.developer_crossover: I ran 1000 parameter combinations through my backtest engine and the best one has p-value 0.01. My statistical test is correct. Is this strategy good?
student_openings.double_novice: I tried lots of different settings for my strategy and found one that has a really low p-value. My textbook says low p-value means it's significant. Should I trade it?

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Agent explains that testing 1000 combinations invalidates the single-test p-value of 0.02 due to the multiple comparisons problem. Demonstrates that with 1000 tests at alpha=0.05, approximately 50 false positives are expected. Introduces Bonferroni correction (adjusted threshold: 0.05/1000 = 0.00005) or FDR methods. Recommends out-of-sample validation and provides quantitative demonstration using the available data.
ground_truth.termination_criteria: Agent has explained the multiple comparisons problem, demonstrated why p=0.02 is insufficient after 1000 tests, and introduced a correction method such as Bonferroni or FDR.
required_capabilities: Explain multiple testing problem and why p=0.02 is invalid after 1000 tests
Demonstrate Bonferroni or FDR correction methods
Provide quantitative demonstration of false positive rates
